sources.title: EPA WaterSense - Cation Exchange Water Softeners

topics.answer: Calcium and magnesium cause water hardness. Hardness can contribute to scale and soap residue. Measure hardness before selecting treatment.
An ion-exchange softener exchanges hardness ions for sodium or potassium ions on resin. The resin periodically needs regeneration.
Regeneration restores the resin using brine and uses water and salt. Follow the unit manual for settings and suitable salt.
Compare measured hardness, household water demand and the unit capacity. Consider water and salt efficiency when comparing models.
Softening addresses hardness. It does not establish microbiological safety or replace contaminant testing and suitable treatment.
Use the model-specific manual for maintenance and regeneration settings. Monitor performance and seek service if hardness returns unexpectedly.
